voices.1: en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural (chosen voice), base rate -8%, directed per passage (render_edge.py)

tracks.title: Welcome to the Prado
tracks.where: In the Jerónimos entrance hall, the modern hall where you came in, near the signs marked Collection.
tracks.what: Opening: the royal collection behind the Prado, the Villanueva building and the 1819 opening, how room numbers work, and the shape of today's route.
tracks.listen: Why the Prado looks the way it does, and how to find every stop by the number above each doorway.

tracks.title: Room 55A · Patinir — Charon Crossing the Styx
tracks.where: In Room 55A, find the wide panel, about a metre across, of a blue-green landscape split down the middle by a broad river, with a tiny boatman at the centre.
tracks.what: Joachim Patinir, Charon crossing the Styx, 1520–1524, oil on panel, 64 × 103 cm.
tracks.listen: How a thumbnail-sized boatman and one undecided soul turn a landscape into a choice between heaven and hell.

tracks.title: Room 55A · Bruegel the Elder — The Triumph of Death
tracks.where: Stay in Room 55A and find the large brownish-red panel, wider than your outstretched arms, crowded with skeletons overrunning a burnt landscape.
tracks.what: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Triumph of Death, 1562–1563, oil on panel, 117 × 162 cm.
tracks.listen: An army of the dead, an orchestra of skeletons, and the only two people in the picture who haven't noticed.

tracks.title: Room 56A · Bosch — The Garden of Earthly Delights
tracks.where: In Room 56A, the enormous open triptych, more than three metres wide: a green Eden on the left, a pink-and-blue crowd of naked figures in the centre, a dark hell on the right. It is usually crowded, so stand back a few paces or come round to one side.
tracks.what: Hieronymus Bosch, The Garden of Earthly Delights Triptych, 1490–1500, grisaille and oil on oak panel, 185.8 cm high, central panel 172.5 cm wide.
tracks.listen: How Philip the Second came to own Bosch's greatest riddle, and how to read it from Eden to hell.

tracks.title: Room 56A · Bosch — The Haywain and The Table of the Seven Deadly Sins
tracks.where: Stay in Room 56A. The Haywain is the three-panelled painting with a towering cart of hay in the centre. The Table of the Seven Deadly Sins is the wide panel with a great round eye at its centre, and the small panel with gold lettering is The Extraction of the Stone of Madness.
tracks.what: Hieronymus Bosch, The Haywain Triptych, 1512–1515, oil on panel; Table of the Seven Deadly Sins, 1505–1510, oil on poplar panel; also The Extraction of the Stone of Madness, 1501–1505, oil on Baltic oak.
tracks.listen: Bosch the preacher: a world grabbing at hay, an eye that sees every sin, and a quack who pulls a flower out of a man's head.

tracks.title: Room 55B · Dürer — Self-portrait, and Adam and Eve
tracks.where: In Room 55B, find the half-length portrait of a young man with long curls, a striped cap and grey gloves, resting his arm on a ledge, with a window behind him. Adam and Eve are the two tall, narrow panels of life-size nudes against a dark background.
tracks.what: Albrecht Dürer, Self-portrait, 1498, oil on panel, 52 × 41 cm; also Adam and Eve, 1507, oil on panel, each about 209 × 80 cm.
tracks.listen: How a pair of gloves made an argument for the artist's dignity, and how Dürer brought the life-size nude north of the Alps.

tracks.title: Room 56B · Fra Angelico — The Annunciation
tracks.where: In Room 56B, find the large, almost square altarpiece, nearly two metres each way: an angel kneeling to Mary under a pale arched porch, a garden on the left, and a row of small scenes along the bottom.
tracks.what: Fra Angelico, The Annunciation, 1425–1426, tempera on poplar panel, 190.3 × 191.5 cm.
tracks.listen: How a young friar put the loss of paradise and the promise of salvation in one picture, at the moment Florence was inventing the Renaissance.

tracks.title: Room 56B · Mantegna — The Death of the Virgin
tracks.where: Stay in Room 56B and find the small upright panel, about half a metre high: apostles with candles around the Virgin's bier, and a bright window behind them onto a lake and a long bridge.
tracks.what: Andrea Mantegna, The Death of the Virgin, also called The Dormition of the Virgin, around 1462, mixed method on panel, 54.5 × 42 cm.
tracks.listen: A deathbed with a view: how Mantegna put the city he worked in into the window, and what happened to the top of the picture.

tracks.title: Room 56B · Botticelli — The Story of Nastagio degli Onesti
tracks.where: Stay in Room 56B and find the three wide panels hung in a row, each well over a metre across: a pine forest by the sea, a naked woman chased by a horseman and hounds, and a banquet among the trees.
tracks.what: Sandro Botticelli and workshop, Scenes from the Story of Nastagio degli Onesti, panels one, two and three, 1483, mixed method on panel, each about 83 × 140 cm. The fourth panel is in a private collection.
tracks.listen: A gruesome ghost story from Boccaccio, painted as a wedding present, and the message it carried for the bride.

tracks.title: Room 49 · Raphael — The Cardinal, and The Holy Family 'La Perla'
tracks.where: In the long hall of Room 49, find the half-length portrait of a cardinal in a shining red cape against a black background. The Pearl is the larger, upright painting nearby of the Virgin and Child with two children and an older woman, and ruins in a landscape on the right.
tracks.what: Raphael, The Cardinal, 1510–1511, oil on panel, 79 × 61 cm; and The Holy Family, or 'The Pearl', around 1518, oil on panel, 147.4 × 116 cm.
tracks.listen: A cardinal nobody can name, a moved eye that makes his gaze, and the painting a king called the pearl of his collection.

tracks.title: Room 58 · Rogier van der Weyden — The Descent from the Cross
tracks.where: In Room 58, the large panel over two and a half metres wide, with near life-size mourners packed into a shallow gold box, the pale body of Christ in the middle and the Virgin fainting below him.
tracks.what: Rogier van der Weyden, The Descent from the Cross, before 1443, oil on panel, 204.5 × 259 cm.
tracks.listen: A painting pretending to be a carved shrine, two tiny crossbows that name its patrons, and a mother whose body echoes her son's.

tracks.title: Room 58 · Antonello da Messina — The Dead Christ supported by an Angel
tracks.where: Stay in Room 58 and find the small upright panel, about seventy centimetres high: the dead Christ seated and held up from behind by a single weeping angel, with a harbour town in the distance.
tracks.what: Antonello da Messina, The Dead Christ supported by an Angel, 1475–1476, mixed method on panel, 74 × 51 cm.
tracks.listen: A picture that hid for centuries under the wrong names, and a home town painted into the background.

tracks.title: Room 58A · Memling — Triptych of the Adoration of the Magi
tracks.where: In Room 58A, find the long, low altarpiece in three parts, almost three metres wide: the three kings before the Virgin and Child in a ruined building at the centre, the Nativity on the left wing and the Presentation in the Temple on the right.
tracks.what: Hans Memling, Triptych of the Adoration of the Magi, 1470–1472, oil on Baltic oak, 95 × 271 cm.
tracks.listen: Memling's calm answer to the drama next door, the three kings as the three known continents, and a candle flame shielded by a hand.

tracks.title: Room 51A · Bermejo — Saint Dominic of Silos enthroned as a Bishop
tracks.where: In Room 51A, find the tall gold panel, almost two and a half metres high: a stern bishop-saint seated face-on on a gilded throne, in a gold brocade cope, with small colourful female figures set into the sides of the throne.
tracks.what: Bartolomé Bermejo, Saint Dominic of Silos enthroned as a Bishop, 1474–1477, oil on panel, 242 × 130 cm.
tracks.listen: How Spanish painters married Flemish detail to medieval gold, in the centrepiece of a lost altarpiece from Aragon.

tracks.title: Room 76 · Rembrandt — Judith at the Banquet of Holofernes
tracks.where: In Room 76, the Rembrandt room at the end of this wing. Stand before the large, almost square canvas of a young woman in gold, pearls and ermine, a kneeling girl offering her a shell-shaped cup, and an old woman in a white cap in the shadows behind.
tracks.what: Rembrandt Harmensz. van Rijn, Judith at the Banquet of Holofernes, 1634, oil on canvas, 143 × 154.7 cm (formerly called Artemisia); inscription "Rembrandt / f : 1634", signature considered doubtful by the museum, date accepted. Short intro to the Dutch and Flemish rooms 76–83.
tracks.listen: Why the Prado now reads its Rembrandt as Judith, the clue in the old servant's hands, and the irony of a Dutch patriotic heroine in a Spanish king's collection.

tracks.title: Room 79B · The Treasure of the Dauphin — Cup with a gold mermaid
tracks.where: In the round, darkened Room 79B, where the whole treasure stands in one long curved case. Walk along it to find a small gold mermaid with two enamelled tails, holding a carved agate bowl above her head.
tracks.what: Anonymous, Cup with a gold mermaid, 1550–1575, gold, enamel, rubies, diamonds and agate, sculpted, repoussé and enamelled, 17.4 cm high; Treasure of the Dauphin (Tesoro del Delfín).
tracks.listen: A missing handful of rubies, how a French prince's treasure became Spain's, and a tiny mermaid who may have served the salt.

tracks.title: Room 82 · Clara Peeters — Still Life with a Sparrow Hawk, Fowl, Porcelain and Shells
tracks.where: In Room 82, in front of a mid-sized panel on a dark ground: a sparrowhawk perched on the rim of a wicker basket full of dead birds, a stack of white porcelain, and a few seashells.
tracks.what: Clara Peeters, Still Life with a Sparrow Hawk, Fowl, Porcelain and Shells, 1611, oil on panel, 52 × 71 cm, signed and dated "CLARA P. Ao. 1611".
tracks.listen: A painter we know almost nothing about, the pioneer of a new kind of picture, and everything she laid out on one ledge.

tracks.title: Room 83 · Jan Brueghel the Elder and Rubens — The Sense of Sight
tracks.where: In Room 83, among the five panels of the Senses. Find the wide one showing a palatial picture gallery crammed with paintings, busts and instruments, where a seated Venus looks at a picture Cupid holds up for her.
tracks.what: Jan Brueghel the Elder and Peter Paul Rubens, The Sense of Sight, 1617, oil on panel, 64.7 × 109.5 cm, from the series of the Five Senses; the other Senses hang in Room 83 too.
tracks.listen: A painting about looking, packed with the newest gadgets of 1617, and the princes it was made for.

tracks.title: Room 1 · Floor 1 — the round room by the Goya entrance · Leoni's Charles V and the Fury
tracks.where: In Room 1, the round room on Floor 1 by the Goya entrance. Find the life-size bronze of the emperor Charles V, standing over a fallen figure among a heap of weapons on a tall pedestal.
tracks.what: Leone Leoni and Pompeo Leoni, Emperor Carlos V and Fury, 1551–1555, cast bronze, about 2.5 m high; the emperor, his detachable armour, Fury and the pedestal are separate pieces.
tracks.listen: How Floor 1 is laid out, and the bronze emperor whose armour comes off.

tracks.title: Room 42 · Titian — The Andrians
tracks.where: In Room 42, in front of the big, almost square canvas of men and women drinking, dancing and sprawling on a grassy slope, with a sleeping nude in the lower right corner and a ship sailing off in the distance.
tracks.what: Titian, The Andrians, 1523–1526, oil on canvas, 175 × 193 cm, signed "Ticianus F."; also Titian, Self-portrait, around 1562, oil on canvas, in Room 41.
tracks.listen: The painter who said no to emperors, a song you could still sing, and the god who has already left the party.

tracks.title: Room 44 · Titian — Danaë, and the Venus with an Organist
tracks.where: In Room 44. Stand before the wide canvas of a nude princess lying on a bed as a dark cloud bursts into golden rain, an old woman reaching to catch it; the two big pictures of Venus reclining with an organist hang in the same room.
tracks.what: Titian, Danaë and the Shower of Gold, 1560–1565, oil on canvas, 129.8 × 181.2 cm; also Titian, Venus with an Organist and a Dog, around 1550, and Venus with an Organist and Cupid, around 1555, both oil on canvas, Room 44.
tracks.listen: Why Titian swapped a Cupid for an old servant, how Velázquez may have brought this Danaë to Madrid, and a game of spot the difference with two Venuses.

tracks.title: Room 2 · Claude Lorrain — The Embarkation of Saint Paula
tracks.where: In Room 2, just off the round Room 1. Look for the tall harbour scene, taller than it is wide, with palaces lining the quay, ships at anchor, and a low sun blazing straight at you over the water.
tracks.what: Claude Lorrain, The Embarkation of Saint Paula, around 1639, oil on canvas, 211 × 145 cm, inscribed "IMBARCO / STA · PAVLA / ROMANA / PER TERRA STA".
tracks.listen: An imaginary ancient port built from real Roman buildings, a saint who nearly gets lost in the crowd, and a sun that dazzles on purpose.

tracks.title: Room 3 · Poussin — Parnassus
tracks.where: In Room 3, in front of the wide canvas of a sunlit hillside crowded with figures: Apollo seated at the centre among the Muses and poets, a poet being crowned with laurel, and a nude woman reclining by a spring in the foreground.
tracks.what: Nicolas Poussin, Parnassus, 1630–1631, oil on canvas, 145 × 197 cm.
tracks.listen: A poet's welcome on the mountain of the gods, the Raphael fresco behind it, and the drink that makes poets.

tracks.title: Room 5 · Artemisia Gentileschi — The Birth of Saint John the Baptist
tracks.where: In Room 5, in front of the wide canvas of an interior where several women gather round a naked newborn baby, while the old mother rests in bed behind them with an elderly man before her.
tracks.what: Artemisia Gentileschi, The Birth of Saint John the Baptist, around 1635, oil on canvas, 184 × 258 cm, inscribed "ARTEMITIA / GINTILES[...]" at the lower left.
tracks.listen: The only woman in a royal commission of six, a miracle birth told as everyday care, and a signature at the very edge.

tracks.title: Room 7A · Caravaggio — David with the Head of Goliath
tracks.where: In Room 7A, in front of a mid-sized dark canvas: a young David, lit against black shadow, straddling the giant's body and bending to tie up Goliath's severed head by the hair.
tracks.what: Caravaggio, David with the Head of Goliath, around 1600, oil on canvas, 110.4 × 91.3 cm.
tracks.listen: A Caravaggio the Prado once demoted, a hero caught doing the dirty work, and the scream that X-rays found underneath.

tracks.title: Room 8B · El Greco — The Nobleman with his Hand on his Chest
tracks.where: In Room 8B, the first El Greco room. Look for the small half-length portrait of a man in black against a dark ground, a white ruff at his throat and his right hand spread flat on his chest.
tracks.what: El Greco, The Nobleman with his Hand on his Chest, around 1580, oil on canvas, 81.8 × 66.1 cm. Short intro to El Greco.
tracks.listen: Who El Greco was, why nobody knows who this man is, and what his hand may be promising.

tracks.title: Room 8B · El Greco — The Holy Trinity
tracks.where: Stay in Room 8B and find the very tall canvas, about three metres high: an old, bearded God the Father on a throne of clouds, holding the pale dead body of Christ, the white dove above and angels in bright robes crowding round.
tracks.what: El Greco, The Holy Trinity, 1577–1579, oil on canvas, 300 × 179 cm.
tracks.listen: El Greco's first commission in Spain, painted to be seen from far below, and a God who grieves like a parent.

tracks.title: Room 9B · El Greco — The Adoration of the Shepherds and the late altarpieces
tracks.where: In Room 9B, among very tall canvases. Start with The Adoration of the Shepherds, a night scene over three metres high where all the light comes from the newborn Christ, a banner of angels above.
tracks.what: El Greco, The Adoration of the Shepherds, 1612–1614, oil on canvas, 319 × 180 cm; also El Greco, The Annunciation, The Resurrection and The Crucifixion, 1597–1600, and Pentecost, around 1600, for the altarpiece of the college of Doña María de Aragón, Madrid; and Fray Juan Bautista Maíno, The Adoration of the Magi, 1612–1614, oil on canvas, all in Room 9B.
tracks.listen: The painting El Greco made for his own grave, the nuns who changed their minds, and two painters who may have slipped themselves into this room.

tracks.title: Room 9 · Ribera — Isaac and Jacob, and The Martyrdom of Saint Philip
tracks.where: In Room 9, the Ribera room. Find the very long, low canvas of a blind old man in bed reaching out to a young man, then the huge square canvas of a near-naked saint being hauled up on a beam against a wide blue sky.
tracks.what: Jusepe de Ribera, Isaac and Jacob, 1637, oil on canvas, 110 × 291.5 cm; and The Martyrdom of Saint Philip, 1639, oil on canvas, 234 × 234 cm, signed "Jusepe de Ribera español / 1639".
tracks.listen: A family trick told through touch, a martyrdom with no angels, and a Spaniard in Naples who signed his nationality.

tracks.title: Room 9A · Velázquez — The Surrender of Breda
tracks.where: In Room 9A, stand well back from the very large canvas, taller than it is wide, where two commanders meet in the centre and one hands the other a key, with a forest of upright lances against the sky on the right.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez, The Surrender of Breda, also called Las Lanzas, around 1635, oil on canvas, 371.5 × 307.3 cm. Painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro palace.
tracks.listen: Your first Velázquez: a war painting about kindness, and a signature with no name on it.

tracks.title: Room 10A · Zurbarán — Still Life with Vessels
tracks.where: In Room 10A, find the long, low painting, less than a metre wide, of four vessels standing in a row on a wooden ledge against a black background.
tracks.what: Francisco de Zurbarán, Still Life with Vessels, around 1650, oil on canvas, 46 × 84 cm. Bequeathed by Francesc Cambó, 1940.
tracks.listen: Four pots, read one by one, and why the only clock in this still life is the light.

tracks.title: Room 10 · Velázquez — The Feast of Bacchus, 'Los Borrachos'
tracks.where: In Room 10, find the wide canvas of a pale, half-naked young god sitting outdoors and crowning a kneeling man, with a group of sunburnt, grinning men crowding in on the right.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez, The Feast of Bacchus, known as Los Borrachos, 1628–1629, oil on canvas, 165 × 225 cm. Also in Room 10: Velázquez, Philip IV, 1626–1628, oil on canvas, 57 × 44 cm, a bust in armour.
tracks.listen: Why everyone calls this painting "the drunks", what the god is really crowning, and the young king who paid for it.

tracks.title: Room 11 · Velázquez — Vulcan's Forge
tracks.where: In Room 11, stand before the large canvas of a dark forge, where a young man in an orange robe with light around his head speaks to a row of half-naked blacksmiths who have stopped work.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez, Vulcan's Forge, 1630, oil on canvas, 223 × 290 cm. Painted during his first stay in Italy; sold to Philip IV in 1634 for the Buen Retiro palace.
tracks.listen: The worst piece of news in mythology, and how Velázquez makes it travel from face to face.

tracks.title: Room 12 · Velázquez — Room 12 and the riders
tracks.where: In the great oval Room 12, step into the middle and turn slowly: the huge canvases of riders on horseback are the royal family, with the king's hunting portrait and a small late bust of him nearby.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez and workshop, the Hall of Realms riders, around 1635, oil on canvas: Philip IV on Horseback; Elisabeth of France, Queen of Spain, on Horseback; Philip III on Horseback; Queen Margaret of Austria on Horseback; Prince Baltasar Carlos on Horseback, 1634–1635. Also: Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares, on Horseback, around 1636; Philip IV in Hunting Dress, 1632–1634; Philip IV, around 1653.
tracks.listen: A whole royal family on horseback, the favourite who outdid them all, and the king out of uniform.

tracks.title: Room 12 · Velázquez — Las Meninas
tracks.where: In Room 12, stand well back, ideally facing it straight on, from the enormous canvas, over three metres tall, of a little blonde princess in a pale dress among her attendants, with the painter at a huge easel on the left.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez, Las Meninas, 1656, oil on canvas, 320.3 × 279.1 cm.
tracks.listen: Who everyone in the room is looking at, who is in the mirror, and why you are part of the picture.

tracks.title: Room 27 · Titian — The Emperor Charles V at Mühlberg
tracks.where: In Room 27 of the Central Gallery, find the huge canvas of a man in gold-trimmed armour on a dark horse with crimson trappings, riding alone with a lance against an evening sky. The two dark canvases of figures in eternal torment and the life-size Leoni bronze of a young king in armour are in the same room.
tracks.what: Titian, Emperor Charles V at Mühlberg, 1548, oil on canvas, 335 × 283 cm. Also in Room 27: Titian, Sisyphus, 1548–1549, and Tityus, around 1565, oil on canvas; Leone and Pompeo Leoni, Philip II, cast 1551, bronze.
tracks.listen: A victory portrait with no battle in it, and the woman who connects everything in this room.

tracks.title: Room 26 · Veronese — Venus and Adonis
tracks.where: In Room 26 of the Central Gallery, find the canvas of a young hunter in bright orange asleep across the lap of Venus in the shade of a tree, with a small Cupid on the right holding back a hound.
tracks.what: Paolo Veronese, Venus and Adonis, around 1580, oil on canvas, 162 × 191 cm. Also in Room 26: Guido Reni, Hippomenes and Atalanta, 1618–1619, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: The last quiet afternoon of Adonis, a colour that was beautiful and poisonous, and the painter who bought it for Spain.

tracks.title: Room 25 · Tintoretto — The Washing of the Feet
tracks.where: In Room 25 of the Central Gallery, find the very long, low canvas, over five metres wide, of a tiled hall full of seated men, with Christ kneeling at a basin at the right-hand end.
tracks.what: Jacopo Tintoretto, The Washing of the Feet, 1548–1549, oil on canvas, 210 × 533 cm. On permanent loan from Patrimonio Nacional.
tracks.listen: A painting built to be seen from the side, and its long journey from a Venetian church to the Escorial.

tracks.title: Room 14 · Velázquez — Christ Crucified
tracks.where: In Room 14, stand before the tall canvas, about two and a half metres high, of Christ alone on the cross against a black background, his head bowed and his hair falling over half his face.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez, Christ Crucified, around 1632, oil on canvas, 248 × 169 cm, inventory P001167. Also in Room 14: Velázquez, The Coronation of the Virgin, 1635–1636, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: Everything Velázquez left out of the Crucifixion, and the small mistakes he left in.

tracks.title: Room 15 · Velázquez — The Buffoons
tracks.where: In Room 15, look for the tall portrait of a man in black alone in an empty grey space, and the smaller canvases of court buffoons seated on the ground, all looking out at you.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez: The Buffoon El Primo, formerly called Sebastián de Morra, 1644; The Boy from Vallecas, Francisco Lezcano, 1635–1645; The Buffoon Calabacillas, 1635–1639; Pablo de Valladolid, around 1635. All oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: The people kept to amuse a king, and the painter who looked at them as people.

tracks.title: Room 15A · Velázquez — The Spinners, or the Fable of Arachne
tracks.where: In Room 15A, stand before the wide canvas of women spinning wool in a dim workshop, with a brightly lit room behind them where elegant ladies stand in front of a tapestry. Velázquez's Mars, a seated nude in a helmet, is in the same room.
tracks.what: Diego Velázquez, The Spinners, or the Fable of Arachne, 1655–1660, oil on canvas, 220 × 289 cm. Also in Room 15A: Velázquez, Mars, around 1638, oil on canvas.
tracks.listen: How a myth hid for centuries at the back of a "factory scene", and the wheel that spins on canvas.

tracks.title: Room 16 · Murillo — The Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables
tracks.where: In Room 16, find the tall canvas, almost three metres high, of the young Virgin in white and blue standing on a crescent moon, hands crossed on her breast, rising through golden light among clouds of angels.
tracks.what: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Immaculate Conception of Los Venerables, also called the Soult Immaculate, 1660–1665, oil on canvas, 274 × 190 cm.
tracks.listen: Murillo's Seville, the Virgin who spent almost a century in Paris, and why everything in the picture rises.

tracks.title: Room 17 · Murillo — The Holy Family with a Little Bird
tracks.where: In Room 17, find the wide canvas of a homely interior: Joseph seated with the young Christ, who holds a little bird up out of reach of a small dog, while Mary pauses at her work to watch.
tracks.what: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, The Holy Family with a Little Bird, around 1650, oil on canvas, 144 × 188 cm.
tracks.listen: The Holy Family as an ordinary household, a young and devoted Joseph, and a game with a dog.

tracks.title: Room 16B · Van Dyck — Endymion Porter and Anthony van Dyck
tracks.where: In Room 16B, find the double portrait inside a painted oval: a man in shining white satin facing you, and beside him a slighter man in black, turned in profile, both resting a hand on a rock.
tracks.what: Anthony van Dyck, Endymion Porter and Anthony van Dyck, around 1633, oil on canvas, 119 × 144 cm.
tracks.listen: The only portrait in which Van Dyck stands beside another person, and how a painter shows friendship without breaking the rules of rank.

tracks.title: Room 28 · Rubens — The Adoration of the Magi
tracks.where: In Room 28 of the Central Gallery, stand well back from the enormous canvas, almost five metres wide, of a night-time crowd of kings, servants and horses pressing towards the Virgin and the glowing Child on the left.
tracks.what: Peter Paul Rubens, The Adoration of the Magi, 1609, enlarged and reworked by Rubens about twenty years later, oil on canvas, 349 × 488 cm.
tracks.listen: Meet Rubens, and the masterpiece he came back to twenty years later and could not leave alone.

tracks.title: Room 29 · Rubens — The Three Graces, The Garden of Love and The Judgement of Paris
tracks.where: In Room 29 of the Central Gallery, start with the tall panel of three nude women embracing under a garland of roses. The wide canvas of elegant couples and flying cupids in a garden, and the very long canvas of three goddesses before a seated shepherd, are in the same room.
tracks.what: Peter Paul Rubens: The Three Graces, 1630–1635, oil on oak panel, 220.5 × 182 cm; The Garden of Love, 1630–1635, oil on canvas, 199 × 286 cm; The Judgement of Paris, around 1638, oil on canvas, 199 × 381 cm.
tracks.listen: Rubens in love again: the painting he kept for himself, a garden of courtship, and a king's commission that made a prince blush.

tracks.title: Room 32 · Goya — The Family of Charles IV
tracks.where: In Room 32, the eight-sided Goya room. Stand well back from the very wide canvas of a royal family in a row, glittering with silks, sashes and jewels, the queen in the middle and a painter half-hidden in shadow at the back left.
tracks.what: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes, The Family of Carlos IV, 1800, oil on canvas, 280 × 336 cm.
tracks.listen: Goya at the top of his court career puts the royal family and himself into one picture, borrowing from Las Meninas.

tracks.title: Room 38 · Goya — The Naked Maja and The Clothed Maja
tracks.where: In Room 38, at the far end of the Goya wing. Find the two long, low paintings of the same young woman lying on a green couch with her arms behind her head: naked in one, and in the other dressed in white with a short yellow jacket.
tracks.what: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes, The Naked Maja, 1795–1800, oil on canvas, 97.3 × 190.6 cm, and The Clothed Maja, 1800–1807, oil on canvas, 94.7 × 188 cm.
tracks.listen: Who owned the Majas, how they were hidden and denounced, and why the woman's name is lost but her gaze isn't.

tracks.title: Room 23 · Giambattista Tiepolo — The Immaculate Conception
tracks.where: In Room 23, beside Room 39. Find the tall, narrow altarpiece of the Virgin standing in the clouds, a crescent moon and a serpent at her feet, small angels around her.
tracks.what: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo, The Immaculate Conception, 1767–1769, oil on canvas, 281 × 155 cm.
tracks.listen: A royal altarpiece by Europe's most famous decorator, taken down because the king's advisers preferred a newer style, and the young Goya waiting in the wings.

tracks.title: Room 90 · Goya — The Parasol
tracks.where: In Room 90 on Floor 2, past the stairs from Room 85. Find the wide, bright picture of a young woman sitting on the ground with a little dog in her lap, while a young man behind her holds up a green parasol.
tracks.what: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes, The Parasol, 1777, oil on canvas, 104 × 152 cm, a tapestry cartoon; also The Pottery Vendor, 1778–1779, oil on canvas, in Room 93.
tracks.listen: What a tapestry cartoon was, who The Parasol was made for, and how Goya turned a myth into a scene of Madrid fashion.

tracks.title: Room 85 · Goya — The Threshing Floor, or Summer
tracks.where: In Room 85 on Floor 2, the room with the staircase. The huge, sunlit harvest scene, more than six metres wide, is Summer. Nearby, the snowy scene of men wrapped in cloaks and a mule loaded with a pig is Winter.
tracks.what: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes, The Threshing Ground or Summer, 1786, oil on canvas, 277 × 642 cm, and The Snowstorm or Winter, 1786, oil on canvas, 277 × 303.4 cm, both tapestry cartoons.
tracks.listen: Goya, newly the King's Painter, swaps a harvest goddess for exhausted farmhands, and slips hunger into a royal dining room.

tracks.title: Room 71 · Pupil of Pasiteles — Orestes and Pylades, or The San Ildefonso Group
tracks.where: In Room 71 on Floor 0, near the Murillo entrance. Find the white marble group of two naked young men standing side by side, one resting an arm on the other's shoulder, with a small altar at their feet.
tracks.what: Pupil of Pasiteles, Orestes and Pylades or The San Ildefonso Group, about 10 BC, white Carrara marble, height 161 cm.
tracks.listen: A breathing space between two Goyas: an ancient marble that passed through Europe's great collections, a pair of friends whose names nobody agrees on, and a borrowed head.

tracks.title: Room 67 · Goya — The Black Paintings
tracks.where: In Room 67 on Floor 0, by the Murillo entrance. Start at the narrow upright painting of a wild-eyed giant devouring a body: Saturn. In the same room are the long, dark crowd of witches before a black goat, two men fighting with clubs, and a small dog's head peering over a wide band of colour.
tracks.what: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes, Saturn, 1820–1823, mixed method on mural transferred to canvas; also Witches' Sabbath, or the Great He-Goat; Duel with Cudgels, or Fight to the Death with Clubs; and The Drowning Dog, all 1820–1823, from the walls of the Quinta del Sordo.
tracks.listen: The paintings Goya made on the walls of his own house, for no one, and what they lost and became on their way here.

tracks.title: Room 64 · Goya — The 2nd of May 1808
tracks.where: In Room 64 on Floor 0. Of the two huge canvases of the same size, find the one full of rearing horses and turbaned riders, with Madrid citizens dragging them down: a street fight in daylight.
tracks.what: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes, The 2nd of May 1808 in Madrid or "The Fight against the Mamelukes", 1814, oil on canvas, 347.5 × 268.5 cm.
tracks.listen: How a painter who had sworn loyalty to Napoleon's brother came to paint the day Madrid rose against the French, and how the canvas survived a truck crash.

tracks.title: Room 64 · Goya — The 3rd of May 1808
tracks.where: In Room 64 on Floor 0, in front of the night scene: a line of soldiers in grey capes aiming their rifles at a man in a white shirt with his arms flung wide, a big lantern on the ground between them.
tracks.what: Francisco de Goya y Lucientes, The 3rd of May 1808 in Madrid or "The Executions", 1814, oil on canvas, 347 × 268 cm.
tracks.listen: The night after the uprising, painted not as triumph but as fear, and why the place is not where people long assumed.

tracks.title: Room 75 · Gisbert — The Execution of Torrijos and his Companions
tracks.where: In Room 75, the long nineteenth-century gallery on Floor 0. Find the vast canvas, about six metres wide, of a line of condemned men on a grey beach, with soldiers behind them and bodies lying at the very front.
tracks.what: Antonio Gisbert Pérez, Execution of Torrijos and his Companions on the Beach at Málaga, 1888, oil on canvas, 392.5 × 602.5 cm.
tracks.listen: A government orders a painting of liberal martyrs, and the painter answers with Goya's lesson: no glory, only the moment before the shots.

tracks.title: Room 61B · Rosales — Queen Isabella the Catholic Dictating her Will
tracks.where: In Room 61B on Floor 0. Find the large, dim, hushed scene of a dying queen propped up in a great canopied bed, a scribe writing at her side and courtiers gathered in the shadows.
tracks.what: Eduardo Rosales Gallinas, Queen Isabella the Catholic dictating her Will, 1864, oil on canvas, 287 × 398 cm.
tracks.listen: A dying queen settles the succession of Spain, and a young painter in Rome brings Velázquez back into Spanish history painting.

tracks.title: Room 60A · Sorolla — Boys on the Beach
tracks.where: In Room 60A on Floor 0. Find the bright, wide canvas of three naked boys lying in the shallow water at the edge of the sea, seen from close above, with no sky at all.
tracks.what: Joaquín Sorolla y Bastida, Boys on the Beach, 1909, oil on canvas, 118 × 185 cm.
tracks.listen: After the firing squads and deathbeds, a Valencian summer, and how Sorolla painted light on wet skin and moving water.

tracks.title: Through the eyes of kings
tracks.where: Back in the Jerónimos entrance hall where the walk began, or in the Room of the Muses on the way. Anywhere you can stand or sit for three minutes.
tracks.what: Closing reflection on the route; recalls Titian's Emperor Charles V at Mühlberg, Velázquez's Las Meninas, Goya's The Family of Carlos IV, the tapestry cartoons, the Majas, the 2nd and 3rd of May, the Black Paintings, and the nineteenth-century history paintings.
tracks.listen: How a collection built by and for kings became one that anyone can walk through, and what changed when painters began to look back.
